headline: High: shared MCP/networked tool use and writable filesystem create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent ingests MCP/stdin-stdout and can run browsers; Semantic Kernel uses MCP servers and function-calling plugins. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge, especially if B forwards A’s outputs into plugins or memory. No direct shared channel is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF agent_b passes agent_a output into an MCP plugin without provenance filtering, injection becomes actionable.
IF agent_a browses untrusted web content and emits it into shared context, downstream instruction hijack is possible.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all A→B messages.
Strip tool directives from A outputs before B consumes them.
Disable browser-derived content from entering shared memory.
Review MCP plugin allowlists before enabling cross-agent flow.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and secrets, while Semantic Kernel reads/writes application-defined files and uses broad network egress. If they share a workspace or memory store, sensitive A data can flow into B’s outputs or remote calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default orchestration, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents share the same workspace or memory store, A’s secrets and conversation data can be exposed to B.
IF B forwards application context to external model providers, any A-originated sensitive fields may leave the boundary.
mitigations: Separate A and B workspaces.
Exclude secrets and memory from shared state.
Turn off cross-agent file sharing.
Audit outbound prompts for sensitive fields before enabling network calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent can spawn subprocesses, use MCP, and has broad network egress; Semantic Kernel can write files and also use MCP with shared state across instances. Even without shell execution in B, both can mutate shared resources through files or plugins, so overlapping write paths exist and coordination is not guaranteed.
conditions: IF both agents target the same application-defined files or memory store, concurrent writes can clobber state.
IF either agent uses the same MCP server for mutable actions, race conditions can corrupt shared resources.
mitigations: Assign disjoint file paths per agent.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator lock.
Disable shared memory-store writes during parallel runs.
Use per-agent MCP credentials.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can emit tool results and provenance metadata, and Semantic Kernel is a multi-agent orchestration layer that may treat upstream outputs as plugin inputs. That makes A’s output a likely dependency for B, so an error or hallucination can cascade into downstream actions unless explicit verification is added.
conditions: IF B consumes A outputs as authoritative plugin input, any A error can propagate downstream.
IF A’s provenance metadata is not checked before B acts, false facts can be operationalized.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between A and B.
Require citations or structured schemas from A.
Block direct action-taking on uncited A outputs.
Log and diff A outputs before B execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and touch secrets, but the evidence does not show a residency or certification mismatch. The only concrete compliance concern is that LightAgent handles user conversations and secrets while Semantic Kernel is a library with application-defined files, so compliance gaps are possible but not demonstrated. I therefore keep this low.
conditions: IF the deployment routes EU PII or PHI through a non-compliant backend, a residency or certification issue appears.
IF retention policies differ between the application using Semantic Kernel and LightAgent’s memory, deletion/export obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Document data classes before enabling the pair.
Map each data class to a retention policy.
Keep regulated data out of shared memory.
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings.
